result.topic_en: Evaluation of the integral of dx/(x^2(1-x)^2) by partial fractions, with the remark that between the given limits it stays finite as mu grows.
result.transcription:
Führt man die Integration aus,
so erhält man
$\frac{1}{\mu}\int \frac{\partial x}{x^2(1-x)^2} = \frac{1}{\mu}\left(-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{1-x}+2\log x - 2\log(1-x)\right) + \text{Const}$
und folglich [?] zwischen [?] den obigen Grenzen einen Werth,
der mit $\mu$ nicht unendlich groß wird.

$\frac{1}{x^2}+\frac{1}{(1-x)^2}+\left(\frac{2}{x(1-x)}\right.$ $\frac{2}{x}+\frac{2}{1-x}$

methods.what: Partial-fraction decomposition of 1/(x^2(1-x)^2), with 2/(x(1-x)) split as 2/x + 2/(1-x)
